description: The 30 best decks of patch 1.22: the 10 finalists in finals order, then the next 20 decks of the round-robin (picked by round-robin mean), ordered by their win rate against the 10 finalists (`vs_top`, 320 games each); decks within 1 game of each other there are ordered by `vs_good`. Strong AI, no talents. 1 of them is secret (`secret: true`): only the rank and the tier are published. 1 of them is withheld (`withheld: true`, with a `withheld_reason`): its numbers are published, not its cards.

ordering.finalists: ranks 1-10: finals order (mean over the 9 other finalists, head-to-head as the tie-break)
ordering.after_finals: ranks 11-30: the next 20 decks of the round-robin, picked by round-robin mean, ordered by vs_top (320 games each against the 10 finalists)
ordering.near_tie: decks within 1 game of each other on vs_top (a run of such neighbours) are ordered by vs_good

tier_rules.summary: Tiers follow measured separation, not eyeballing. Walking down the rank list, a deck joins the current tier unless the first deck of that tier beats it with 99.9% confidence (z > 3.29); if it does, the deck opens the next tier.
tier_rules.test: difference = mean win rate of the tier leader minus that of the deck, over the same opponents (paired); standard error from the binomial variance of every pair; separated when difference / SE > 3.29 (two-sided 99.9%; stricter than the usual 95% because about 30 sequential comparisons are made, and it keeps the tier count readable).

scales.finals: leader and deck are both finalists: finals matrix, 200 games per pair, mean over the 9 other finalists (their mutual games count once, opposed)
scales.round_robin: at least one is not a finalist: round-robin matrix, 32 games per pair, mean over the 47 other decks of the 48

caveats: No multiple-comparison correction: tiers are a readability aid, and decks inside a tier are not ranked apart with confidence.
Ranks 1-10 (finals field, stronger opponents) and 11-30 (round-robin field) come from different fields; their win rates are not on one scale.
Ranks 11-30 are ordered by their win rate against the top 10 (320 games each, about ±5 points), so neighbours a few points apart are not ranked apart with confidence.
From rank 11 on, the check against the tier leader uses round-robin data (the opponents both decks met, 32 games per pair, so noisy), not the vs top 10 number that orders those ranks.
